owner_creation.analysis: This table_rows c_int owns the last initialized geometry, distinct from capacity; pos_init starts at zero and updates it after clearing changed rows.
owner_creation.invariant: Logical row count tracks initialized table content.
limitations: table_rows records initialized geometry rather than owning rows separately.

aliases_escapes.analysis: Readers copy min(sc_height,table_rows) before scanning; no array reference is returned by the row-count value.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Logical rows limit a scan but do not own its bytes.
limitations: The old row count can admit reads after the table allocation has been freed.

callback_targets.analysis: No callback target lives in this table_rows field; get_scrpos consumes it during ordinary navigation and fatal cleanup through direct calls.
callback_targets.invariant: Row metadata can be read during cleanup reentry.
limitations: Cleanup reaches get_scrpos before successful replacement updates table_rows.

invalidation.analysis: Resize reuse invalidates removed/newly exposed rows before changing the table_rows count; old rows may nevertheless describe a freed array during allocation growth.
invalidation.invariant: Initialized-row history cannot validate retired storage.

mutation_commit.analysis: table_rows changes immediately in the within-capacity branch, but the growth branch assigns it only after ecalloc returns. Failed growth therefore retains the old initialized-row count while table already points to freed storage; the geometry scalar outlives its backing array (M0-MEM-004).
mutation_commit.invariant: Row publication must remain coherent with its backing owner.

release_pair.analysis: The table_rows scalar has no destructor/free pair; clearing rows logically retires positions without releasing array capacity.
release_pair.invariant: Invalidating rows is distinct from freeing the allocation.
limitations: Retiring geometry does not itself free or null the table pointer.

error_cleanup.analysis: table_rows participates directly in the cleanup read guard: get_scrpos uses min(sc_height,table_rows). The ecalloc -> out_of_memory -> quit -> edit(NULL) -> edit_ifile(NULL) -> close_file path can reach that guard before table_rows is updated. With a current tty file and at least two old rows, the count admits reads through freed table (M0-MEM-004).
error_cleanup.invariant: Row bounds do not resolve the growth cleanup hazard.

signals_handoff.analysis: As a mutable global, table_rows's relation to sc_height/table relies on excluded reentry; ordinary resize tests do not establish a handler-safe transaction.
signals_handoff.invariant: Existing M0-MEM-003 and IND-POS-F4 remain open.
limitations: Source-level growth/fatal-cleanup ordering concern is recorded under existing M0-MEM-001; no new runtime proof or fix is claimed. M0-MEM-003 and IND-POS-F4 remain open.

src/pager.rs.relationship: ecalloc failure at src/pager.rs:860-887 enters quit/edit(NULL) at src/pager.rs:948-969 before table_rows can be updated for the new screen height.

src/edit.rs.relationship: close_file invokes get_scrpos at src/edit.rs:899-907 via src/edit.rs:924-927 and src/edit.rs:1078-1083; the position reader uses old table_rows to admit rows during failed-growth cleanup.
